contractSource: Description: "Calculate structural loads for beams and slabs..." Unit System: Metric (kN/m²) or Imperial (psf). Load presets: "Residential Floor — Typical residential building", etc.
groundTruth: Total area load = area × (dead + live + additional). 1 kN/m² = 1,000 N ÷ 4.44822 N/lbf ÷ 10.7639 ft²/m² = 20.885 psf. A preset describes a physical floor, so its loads must mean the same thing in either unit system.

cases.derivation: Residential Floor preset is 3 + 2 + 0.5 = 5.5 kN/m² (dead + live + additional, as the metric preset fills). On 10 m²: 10 × 5.5 = 55 kN.

cases.note: The same physical floor in US units.
cases.derivation: The preset's 5.5 kN/m² in US units is 5.5 × 20.885 = 114.87 psf (for reference, IBC residential live load alone is 40 psf, and 2 kN/m² ≈ 41.8 psf). On 100 ft²: 100 × 114.87 = 11,487 lb. A result near 550 lb would mean 3, 2 and 0.5 were taken as psf.
